strategy: Individual complete-frame edits, replacing rejected atlas candidates

prompts.Left-0:
Edit target Image1: ONE existing bichon desktop-pet sprite, walking LEFT. Repose its FOUR LEGS to the single motion diagram Image2. Near fore: reach forward and LAND. Near hind: support slightly forward of hip. Far fore: planted behind shoulder. Far hind: begins small toe-off behind hip, barely lifted.
Diagram DARK BLUE = camera-near FORE; DARK GREEN = camera-near HIND. Pale colors = far legs. Solid paw dots grounded, hollow dots lifted. The paths describe behavior; preserve original short fluffy limbs and natural joint lengths, don't stretch them to literal stick bones. Keep each paw attached to the same shoulder/hip root, no ownership swaps. Front/hind lifted paws should travel low and smoothly underneath the body. Render this ONE distinct walk phase, not a standing pose.
Change legs only. Preserve exact original head shape and size, three-quarter face angle toward viewer, tongue smile, long ear hair, compact torso, white curly coat, red patterned collar/gold bell and fluffy curled tail, all in the original position and scale. Keep gentle fur texture and clean alpha edges. Output ONE 1024x1024 RGBA sprite, genuinely transparent background, no floor, shadow, glow, fog or semitransparent gray backdrop. No diagram/text.
